svg.text: AKS image pull failure — root-cause review
Cluster cannot pull from Azure Container Registry
Current-state topology of the customer's AKS-to-ACR path as deployed today. Pods are stuck in
ImagePullBackOff. Two independent blockers were found: the registry has public network access
disabled with no private endpoint in the cluster vnet (no network path), and the kubelet identity
has no AcrPull role assignment on the registry (no authorization). Both must be fixed before pulls
succeed.
rg-aks-prod
resource-group

g.title: vnet-aks · 10.10.0.0/16 Cluster virtual network. Contains only the node subnet — there is no private endpoint subnet and no privatelink.azurecr.io private DNS zone linked to this vnet.

svg.text: snet-aks-nodes · 10.10.1.0/24
subnet
rg-shared-services
resource-group

g.title: kubelet identity (Managed Identities) The kubelet's user-assigned managed identity, used to request pull tokens from ACR. It currently has no role assignments scoped to the registry, so even with a working network path pulls would fail authorization with 401 Unauthorized. AcrPull on ACR: not assigned

aks-prod-cluster (Kubernetes Services) Production AKS cluster. Workload pods reference images in acrcustomerprod.azurecr.io; every pull fails. After both findings are remediated, validate end-to-end with 'az aks check-acr --acr acrcustomerprod.azurecr.io'. Pod status: ImagePullBackOff ACR integration: not attached

acrcustomerprod (Container Registries) Container registry holding the workload images. Public network access is disabled (good intent), but no private endpoint was ever created, so the registry is unreachable from everywhere — including the cluster vnet. Note that Private Link requires the Premium SKU. Public network access: Disabled Private endpoints: none

svg.text: pull auth via kubelet identity
image pull — failing
Findings

text.tspan: — No network path from AKS to ACR

svg.text: Public network access on acrcustomerprod is Disabled but no private endpoint exists in vnet-aks (and no
privatelink.azurecr.io DNS zone is linked), so the registry is unreachable from the nodes. This is the direct cause
of the ImagePullBackOff outage.
Fix: Create a private endpoint for the registry in vnet-aks (az network private-endpoint create
--private-connection-resource-id <acr-id> --group-id registry) and link the privatelink.azurecr.io private DNS
zone to the vnet via a DNS zone group.
The kubelet's managed identity has no AcrPull role assignment on the registry. Once the network path is restored,
pulls will still fail with 401 Unauthorized until this is granted.
Fix: Run 'az aks update -g rg-aks-prod -n aks-prod-cluster --attach-acr acrcustomerprod' (or 'az role assignment
create --assignee <kubelet-identity-client-id> --role AcrPull --scope <acr-resource-id>').

text.tspan: — Private Link requires ACR Premium SKU

svg.text: Private endpoints are only supported on the Premium tier. Verify the registry SKU before creating the endpoint;
Basic/Standard registries must be upgraded first.
Fix: Check with 'az acr show -n acrcustomerprod --query sku.name' and, if needed, 'az acr update -n acrcustomerprod
--sku Premium'.

text.tspan: — Validate the fix with az aks check-acr

svg.text: After both blockers are remediated, the built-in connectivity check confirms DNS resolution, network reachability,
and pull authorization in one command.
Fix: Run 'az aks check-acr -g rg-aks-prod -n aks-prod-cluster --acr acrcustomerprod.azurecr.io', then restart the
failing deployments.
